overall: The AG found no violation: the May 20 meeting notice was posted May 15, more than 48 hours ahead, and the executive session notice was adequate. It declined to review a later-raised revised-notice posting issue, and only reminded the Committee of its obligations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee held its May 20, 2019 meeting without posting 48 hours' prior notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee posted notice of the May 20 meeting at least 48 hours prior on May 15, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Notice for the executive session on collective bargaining strategy listed bargaining units but named non-union personnel only through a separate link, before later revisions added names.
allegations.key_passage: When convening in executive session pursuant to Purpose 2 or Purposed, a public body must identify the collective bargaining unit or nonunion personnel with whom it will be negotiating, if doing so will not compromise the lawful purpose for secrecy.

allegations.summary: On request for further review, complainant said revised notices omitted the date and time the original notice was posted; AG did not review because it was not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this allegation was not clearly raised in the original complaint and thus we do not review its merits.
